idiom_name: record with init-only properties + object initializer + with expression
implementation_notes: C# absorbed this pattern's job into the language: new EmailRequest { To = t, Subject = s } names every value at the call site, members that are not mentioned keep their initializers, and init accessors (C# 9) keep the result immutable once the initializer completes; required members (C# 11) make the compiler reject an initializer that omits them, and with expressions cover the partial-override case a builder is reused for. The classic fluent builder still earns its place when construction is staged, when cross-field validation must run once before the object exists, or when the result may be one of several subtypes - the framework's own examples are ASP.NET Core's WebApplicationBuilder and EF Core's ModelBuilder.
pitfalls: An object initializer cannot enforce rules spanning fields (Bcc requires a confidential subject): every combination that compiles is constructed, so such rules belong in the constructor or a Build() method - required only checks presence.
with performs a shallow copy: a mutable collection or reference-typed member is shared between the original and the copy unless the record defines a custom copy constructor.
Properties left as set instead of init produce a mutable object, which is the JavaBeans inconsistency problem wearing C# syntax.

variants.name: Hand-written fluent builder for staged or validated construction
variants.idiom_name: nested Builder class with chainable With* methods and Build()
variants.implementation_notes: For staged construction, cross-field validation or a polymorphic product, write the classic structure by hand: a (usually nested) builder class whose methods mutate the accumulated state and return this, and a Build() that validates and calls the product's constructor. This is the shape ASP.NET Core uses for the host (WebApplicationBuilder) and EF Core for models (ModelBuilder); keep it only where the record/with form cannot express the rules, and make the builder the only public way in.
variants.code_sketch:
var email = new EmailRequestBuilder()
    .WithTo("a@x.dev")
    .WithSubject("Hi")
    .WithCc("audit@x.dev")    // confidential subject derived internally
    .Build();                // throws InvalidOperationException on violations
pitfalls: The builder duplicates the record's member list, and adding a property to the product does not make the builder fail to compile, so the two drift silently.
A mutating builder is not thread-safe and must not be cached: like WebApplicationBuilder it is single-use, and reuse after Build() mixes configurations.
